Rama, Lakshmana, and Sage Vishwamitra walk through the desolate wasteland known as Tataka Van. The forest is unnervingly silent. The trees are twisted; the ground barren.
Rama: Gurudev, why does Tataka carry such hatred? Was she born a monster?

Vishwamitra: No, Rama. She was a Yaksha princess born of a boon from Brahma. She married a powerful prince named Sunda and had two sons, Maricha and Subahu. Sunda was killed by Sage Agastya’s curse. Tataka attempted to kill the sage in her grief and was transformed into a hideous, man-eating cannibal.
Rama (troubled): She is a grieving wife who lost her husband and a mother whose life was destroyed by a curse. How can I strike down a woman driven by sorrow?

Vishwamitra: She is no longer just a grieving wife. The only way to save her soul from this agonising curse is to destroy this physical form. Do not be swayed by her history. Look at the present danger.

Rama takes a deep breath and bows to the sage. He raises his great bow, pulls the heavy bowstring back to his ear, and releases it. A massive boom echoes through the forest. A terrifying roar answers the boom. An enraged Tataka crashes through the tree line.
Rama: Brother, even in this form, she is a woman. Our combat protocol dictates that we must not kill immediately. We shall try to disable her first and hope she will retreat.

Tataka does not slow down. She raises her hands, manipulating the ambient air pressure in the region. A massive vacuum forms, pulling in dirt and dry earth, instantly creating a blinding dust storm. From within the vortex, Tataka hurls massive boulders.

Rama responds with a rapid rain of arrows, intercepting the boulders in mid-air and cutting off her attacking arms. Lakshmana, moving swiftly through the dust, aims carefully and slices off her nose and ears. Despite her wounds, Tataka does not retreat.

Suddenly, her form vanishes into the swirling dust. The temperature rapidly drops. Sharp, heavy stones of solid ice begin raining down on the princes and five identical Tatakas appear in the sky, surrounding them.
Lakshmana: How is this possible? She is everywhere!

Vishwamitra: It is an optical illusion! She is using her powers of camouflage to suspend tiny ice crystals in the air and refract the sunlight to project multiple mirages of herself! Rama, she is beyond redemption, and her powers grow stronger at dusk. You must destroy her now!
Rama: If she uses light to hide, I will use sound to find her.

He focusses on a specific, low-frequency vibration echoing beneath the noise of the storm: the rhythmic thumping of Tataka’s heart. He pulls a special arrow from his quiver, designed to whistle at the same frequency as her heartbeat. Once released, the acoustic homing missile tracks the sound waves directly to their source. The arrow vanishes into the dust storm. A second later, a deafening shriek pierces the air. The optical illusions shatter. The dust storm collapses. Tataka falls to the ground.
Vishwamitra: You have brought light back to this forest, Rama. Rest now. Soon we may face bigger problem with her sons.
The Sonic Boom: When an object moves through the air faster than the speed of sound, it creates shockwaves and a thunderous noise. Modern fighter jets do this today.
Atmospheric Manipulation: In Nature, when high-pressure air rushes into a low-pressure area, it creates powerful winds and cyclones.

Acoustic Homing: Sonar sends out sound waves to detect invisible objects underwater by listening to specific frequencies bouncing back to it. Many marine animals, like dolphins and whales, use this to navigate and find food. Modern naval submarines also use a similar technology.

The Myristica Swamps (Kerala, India): Found in tiny pockets like Kulathupuzha and Shendurney, these are actual living fossil ecosystems. Their intertwined, exposed breathing roots (called pneumatophores) rise out of the mud, and their waterlogged, dark canopies create a spooky, prehistoric atmosphere unlike any standard tropical woods.
The Crooked Forest (Poland): A mysterious grove of pine trees that all bend sharply at a 90-degree angle at the base, looking like giant wooden fishhooks.
The Dancing Forest (Rybachii, Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia): A bizarre pine forest where the tree trunks mysteriously contort, twist, and loop into rings and spirals as if they are dancing.
Hoia-Baciu Forest (Romania): Famous for its strangely curved, skeletal trees and eerie silence, it has such a creepy atmosphere that locals often call it the Bermuda Triangle of Transylvania.
What You Need: A large plastic/glass bowl; plastic wrap; a large rubber band; uncooked rice grains or candy sprinkles; metal baking pan; wooden spoon
Step 1: Stretch the plastic wrap tightly over the bowl so that it is completely flat and tight. Secure with the rubber band holding it in place around the rim.
Step 2: Sprinkle a small handful of rice grains or candy sprinkles in the centre of the sheet.
Step 3: Hold the metal baking pan close to the bowl without touching it or the plastic wrap. Now hit the pan hard with the spoon.
Step 4: Watch the rice grains/sprinkles suddenly jump and dance on the plastic wrap.

The Science Behind It: Though invisible, sound is actually a physical wave moving through the air. When you hit the pan, the vibrations push the air molecules outward. These invisible waves travel through the air, hit the tight plastic wrap, and cause it to vibrate at the exact same frequency, making the rice grains/sprinkles jump!
